signals.title: Paco Sanchez: Wenn man nur Party machen will, interessiert mich das nicht
signals.summary: Im Interview von SPEEDWEEK.com erklärt MotoGP-Manager Paco Sanchez, welche Eigenschaften ein Fahrer mitbringen muss, um Weltmeister zu werden – und wann es Zeit ist, getrennte Wege zu gehen. Im zweiten Teil des Interviews von SPEEDWEEK.com-Autor Manuel Pecino erklärt Paco Sanchez, Manager von Joan Mir und Raul Fernandez, nach welchen Kriterien er die Fahrer auswählt, mit denen er zusammenarbeiten will. Was es braucht, um Weltmeister zu werden. Paco. Gehst du auf Fahrer zu, mit denen zu zusammenarbeiten willst, oder gehen sie auf sich zu? «Sie suchen immer mich auf. Ich klopfe niemals an die Tür eines Fahrers. Sie rufen immer mich an – entweder sie selbst, ihre Eltern, ein Freund oder ein Verwandter. Jemand ruft mich an und sagt: «Hey, schau mal, ich habe diesen Fahrer und wir würden gerne mit dir zusammenarbeiten.» Ich bewerte dann den Fahrer. Mein Ziel ist es immer, aus meiner Sicht zu verstehen, ob er das Zeug dazu hat, um den Weltmeistertitel zu kämpfen. Wenn ich nicht glaube, dass er das Zeug dazu hat, ziehe ich es vor, nicht mit ihm zusammenzuarbeiten. Geld ist für mich nicht der Antrieb. Es gibt sehr viele Fahrer, die mir ein festes Gehalt angeboten haben, damit ich mit ihnen zusammenarbeite. In meinem Fall ist das Einzige, was mich motiviert, zu gewinnen. Und tatsächlich waren wir mit 90 Prozent der Fahrer, mit denen ich im Laufe meiner gesamten Karriere zusammengearbeitet habe, entweder Weltmeister oder Vize-Weltmeister. Ich konnte mehr als 24 Weltmeistertitel in verschiedenen Disziplinen des Motorsports feiern und sechs oder sieben Vize-WM-Titel. Letztendlich befanden wir uns rund 30-mal im Kampf um die Weltmeisterschaft – in verschiedenen Disziplinen des Motorsports. Das ist es, was mich motiviert. Das ist es, was mich dazu bringt, weiterhin mit Begeisterung zu arbeiten, weiterhin gerne zu reisen – trotz der ganzen Opfer.» Welche Eigenschaften analysierst du, bevor du zustimmst, einen Fahrer zu vertreten? «Ich schaue mir das Umfeld des Fahrers an, analysiere es, betrachte seine bisherige Karriere und schaue, was er geleistet hat. Ich schaue mir sein Potenzial an und analysiere etwas, das für mich sehr wichtig ist: seine Einstellung. Warum die Einstellung? Weil ich keine Lust habe, mit einem Fahrer zu arbeiten, der schon zu selbstsicher ist, der wenig Lust zum Arbeiten mitbringt und glaubt, alles allein auf sein angeborenes Talent stützen zu können. Ich glaube, dass ein Fahrer oder jeder Champion drei entscheidende Dinge vereinen muss: Das eine ist angeborenes Talent – das hat man von Geburt an, das kann man sich nicht aneignen. Das zweite ist die Arbeit: Er muss bereit sein, zu arbeiten und Opfer zu bringen. Und drittens ist da die Einstellung. Die Einstellung, dass er Weltmeister werden will und dies über alles andere stellt. Wenn die Prioritäten bei den Frauen, den Partys, Ibiza, den Autos und so weiter liegen, interessiert mich das nicht. Denn selbst wenn er das Talent und die Arbeitsbereitschaft hat, wird er nicht gewinnen. Niemals. Oder er wird einen Titel gewinnen und danach in den Hintergrund geraten. Wenn man also diese drei Aspekte vereint, hat man es in der Regel mit jemandem zu tun, der um den Weltmeistertitel kämpfen wird. Ob man ihn am Ende gewinnt oder nicht, ist manchmal eine Frage von Details, von Glück. Ich habe viele Vize-Meisterschaften erreicht, die sich für mich wie ein Titel angefühlt haben. Und dann gibt es Meisterschaften, die wir gewonnen haben und bei denen man sagt: Da hatten wir mehr Glück oder es hat einfach so gepasst. Es haben sich bestimmte Umstände ergeben.» Gab es Fahrer, bei denen du dich aufgrund von Meinungsverschiedenheiten über deren Zukunft dazu entschieden hast, die Zusammenarbeit zu beenden? «Ich habe niemals das Handtuch geworfen. Aber natürlich haben wir uns in der Vergangenheit auch von sehr vielen Fahrern getrennt. Nach acht oder neun Jahren haben wir uns zum Beispiel von Pol Espargaro getrennt. Bei seinem Bruder Aleix ging es schon viel früher auseinander. Auch bei Maverick Vinales haben wir nach vier oder fünf Jahren beschlossen, getrennte Wege zu gehen. Und mit Toni Elias hatten wir eine Diskussion über seine Zukunft. Er war der Meinung, er müsse einen bestimmten Weg einschlagen, ich sah das anders. Letztendlich ist er seinen Weg gegangen und ich habe meinen eigenen Weg mit anderen Fahrern eingeschlagen. Aber das Handtuch werfen? Nein. Niemals.» Nach Durststrecke: KTM ist zurück am Podium! signals.title: Born Slippy: WMC builds its most ambitious bike yet
signals.summary: The WMC Mono RR combines aerodynamic efficiency with a supercharged 449cc Yamaha single, with targets of 100hp and a 100kg weight. White Motorcycle Concepts (WMC) has taken on its most ambitious build to date, with WMC claiming that its new Mono RR boasts 16.4 per cent less drag and 77 per cent more downforce than a conventional bike. The Mono RR is a technology demonstrator designed to show how motorcycle aerodynamics and powertrain design could work together to improve performance and efficiency, without changing the familiar riding position of a conventional sports bike. At the heart of the project is WMC's patented aerodynamic duct, which channels air through the centre of the motorcycle rather than forcing it around the bodywork. By reducing the frontal area and allowing air to pass through the bike, the system is designed to reduce drag while also improving aerodynamic stability. WMC has based the Mono RR on the Krämer EVO2 690R, a lightweight track bike that provides a useful benchmark for measuring the benefits of the company's ideas. The original chassis, suspension and brakes have been retained, with modifications made to accommodate the new engine and the all-important duct system. That engine is a 449cc single-cylinder unit derived from the Yamaha YZ450F motocross bike. It uses a reverse-cylinder-head layout, with the intake at the front and exhaust at the rear, helping WMC separate cooler intake air from hot exhaust gases while also creating space for the duct. Rather than leaving the engine in standard trim, WMC has fitted a Rotrex C15-20 supercharger, driven from the crankshaft, along with an intercooler and revised fuel-injection hardware. The aim is to produce comparable performance to the larger 693cc KTM single used in the original Krämer. WMC's initial target is around 75hp, broadly matching the 76hp output of the standard Krämer, with a longer-term goal of increasing power towards 100hp. The company is also targeting a reduction in weight from the donor bike's 125kg down to 100kg. For now, though, that weight saving remains a development target rather than an accomplishment. According to WMC's computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, the Mono RR reduces aerodynamic drag by 16.4 per cent, cuts lift by 77 per cent and improves thermal management by 16 per cent compared with the conventional Kramer design. The company also estimates that the aerodynamic changes could improve fuel efficiency by seven per cent. The duct has required changes to the front mudguard, fork shrouds and fairing, while extensions around the sides of the bike are intended to smooth airflow around the rider's legs. WMC says those extensions reduce rider-related drag by 36 per cent compared with the standard Krämer. Despite the extensive aerodynamic work, the Mono RR retains the donor bike's seat height, riding position, wheelbase and chassis geometry. By doing that, WMC effectively ratifies that the technology could be applied to existing motorcycle platforms without requiring manufacturers to develop entirely new chassis. The next stage is to validate the CFD results through physical track testing, allowing WMC to compare simulated aerodynamic gains with the bike’s performance in the real world. WMC is an engineering and technology company rather than a motorcycle manufacturer, so the Mono RR is not intended to reach showrooms. Instead, the project is designed to demonstrate technology that could eventually be licensed to established manufacturers, with the potential to improve efficiency and performance across future road and racing motorcycles. That final point noted, we can’t help but wish we could have a go on it! signals.title: Honda updates CBR600RR for 2027 with Fireblade brakes and new TFT display
signals.summary: Honda's 2027 CBR600RR gains Fireblade-derived front brakes, revised aerodynamics and a larger TFT display, while retaining its 599cc inline-four engine. Honda has updated its CBR600RR for 2027, bringing revised front-end styling, new braking hardware and a larger TFT display to its middleweight supersport, while retaining the 599cc inline-four engine that produces 119bhp. The biggest mechanical change is the adoption of Nissin radial-mount, four-piston front brake calipers from the larger CBR1000RR-R Fireblade. They clamp a pair of 310mm floating discs and are paired with a radial-piston master cylinder, with Honda aiming to improve braking performance and control on both road and track. The braking system also gets a revised ABS module derived from the Fireblade, introducing three selectable modes. Standard mode prioritises stability in a wider range of conditions, including wet weather, while Track reduces the intervention of the system by removing rear-wheel lift control. Race mode goes further, disabling rear ABS to allow more aggressive braking, with the system retaining control over front-wheel slip. The CBR600RR's front fairing has also been reworked for 2027, with the previous winglets integrated into the bodywork beneath the headlights. Honda says the revised frontal spoiler retains the previous design's downforce without increasing drag, while also helping to direct airflow away from the rider's arms to reduce buffeting and fatigue. Another change comes in the cockpit, where the previous display is replaced by a five-inch full-colour TFT screen. It includes a shift-up indicator, alongside information such as lap times, lap count and fastest lap, giving riders more useful data for circuit riding. The engine remains a 599cc, 16-valve inline-four producing 119bhp at 14,250rpm and 46.5lb-ft of torque at 11,500rpm. Honda says upgraded camshaft, valve spring and crankshaft materials help manage the forces associated with high engine speeds, while revised inlet ports increase flow capacity by 2.2%. Valve timing has also been adjusted to improve intake efficiency and exhaust gas flow. Electronics continue to include throttle-by-wire, a six-axis inertial measurement unit, nine-level Honda Selectable Torque Control, wheelie control, cornering ABS and rear-lift control. A quickshifter and assist/slipper clutch remain standard, with three preset riding modes and two customisable User modes available. The aluminium twin-spar frame, 41mm Showa Big Piston forks and Unit Pro-Link rear suspension carry over, while kerb weight remains 194kg and seat height is 820mm. Honda will offer the 2027 CBR600RR in Ignition Red HRC TriColour and Matt Ballistic Black Metallic. Three HRC race kits, developed for World Supersport, Superbike and track-day use, will also be available for circuit use only. The 2027 Honda CBR600RR will be priced at £10,999 in the UK, unchanged from the current model. The updated supersport will be available in UK dealerships from January 2027. signals.title: Honda's new CBR500R FOUR gets a four-cylinder engine and E-Clutch
signals.summary: Honda has unveiled the CBR500R FOUR, a new 500cc inline-four sports bike with standard E-Clutch technology and an A2 licence option. Honda has unveiled the CBR500R FOUR, a new middleweight sports bike powered by an all-new 500cc inline-four engine, with standard-fit E-Clutch technology and an A2 licence-friendly version also planned. The 2027 model year machine draws on the Japanese manufacturer's experience with smaller-capacity four-cylinder bikes, including the CB400 SUPER FOUR, which was sold in Japan for more than three decades. The new CBR500R FOUR is intended to bring that engine configuration to a wider audience, combining a high-revving motor with modern electronics and everyday usability. However, the naming could cause a little confusion. Honda already sells a CBR500R, which uses a parallel-twin engine, meaning the new CBR500R FOUR will sit alongside a motorcycle with an almost identical name but a fundamentally different engine layout. The addition of 'FOUR' is therefore an important distinction, particularly for buyers trying to work out which version of the CBR500R they are looking at. The new machine's 500cc DOHC, 16-valve inline-four produces 53.0 kW at 11,000rpm, equivalent to around 73bhp, at 11,000rpm, with peak torque of 47.4Nm arriving at 9,750rpm. The engine has a 12,500rpm redline and uses a ram-air-fed downdraft intake system, with Honda also fitting low-friction cylinder coatings and Diamond-Like Carbon valve lifters. Its 4-2-1 exhaust layout takes inspiration from the 1975 CB400 FOUR, one of Honda's early four-cylinder road bikes. The company says the new engine has been developed to offer a broad spread of power, rather than relying solely on high engine speeds, although the peak power and torque figures suggest riders will still need to work the gearbox to get the best from it. Honda's E-Clutch system comes as standard, allowing the rider to pull away, stop and change gear without operating the clutch lever. The lever remains in place for conventional use, while the system also works with the bike's throttle-by-wire controls to manage rev-matched downshifts. Riders can adjust the system's operation and switch it off if they prefer to use the clutch manually. Three riding modes, Standard, Sport and Urban, are provided, alongside two customisable User settings. These allow adjustments to engine power, engine braking and Honda Selectable Torque Control, the latter being Honda's traction control system. The chassis uses a steel tube diamond-style frame, 41mm KYB upside-down front forks and a Pro-Link rear suspension setup, with an aluminium swingarm. Braking comes from twin 296mm front discs with radial-mount Nissin two-piston calipers, while two-channel ABS is standard. Pirelli Diablo Rosso IV tyres are fitted, and the claimed kerb weight is 189kg. Other equipment includes a five-inch colour TFT display, Honda RoadSync smartphone connectivity, LED lighting and a USB-C charging socket. Seat height is 780mm, while the 14-litre fuel tank is designed to keep the bike practical enough for everyday riding. Honda will offer the CBR500R FOUR in Ignition Red Tricolour and Mat Ballistic Black Metallic, with a 35kW version available for A2 licence holders. The Honda CBR500R FOUR will be priced at £6,999 in the UK, with bikes arriving in dealerships in January 2027. A 35kW version will also be available for A2 licence holders. signals.title: Swindon-based bike dealer Two70 Motorcycles enters administration
signals.summary: Swindon motorcycle dealer Two70 Motorcycles has entered administration after six years of trading, raising further questions about the challenges facing UK bike dealers and the electric motorcycle market. The specialist motorcycle dealer, Two70 Motorcycles, has entered administration following six years of trading. The company behind the brand, J&M Electrobikes, was founded in 2020 and carried bikes from Mutt Motorcycles, Zero, VMoto and Stark Future. With three of those four brands being electric only, it’s not clear whether the difficult UK market for battery-powered bikes was behind the firm’s decline. Adding to the pain for Two70 was the demise of Mutt Motorcycles, which entered administration in March 2025. Mutt primarily produced cafe racer and scrambler bikes that fell into the A1 and A2 classes. Removing those cheap and cheerful yet attractive models from the showroom would likely have hit the brand's profitability. A post on Facebook from the brand, which has since been deleted, indicates that the closure was announced in September and an online sale was held to sell off the remaining stock before the shutters came down. A spokesperson at the time said: “It's with a heavy heart that we will unfortunately be closing Two70 Motorcycles … I'd like to thank everyone for their custom and support." The UK motorcycle market remains a difficult place for dealers, particularly those betting on electric bikes, where high purchase prices, limited demand and questions around charging and range continue to present hurdles. Two70’s closure also follows the collapse of SuperBike Factory, which entered administration earlier this year, underlining the pressures facing businesses across the trade. While the reasons behind Two70’s failure have not been confirmed, its demise is another reminder that finding a sustainable business model in an increasingly competitive market is no easy ride. signals.summary: Norton’s new Manx R superbike has been recognised by none other than Red Dot, after picking up the ‘Best of the Best’ design concept award. Norton’s new 206bhp Manx R superbike has provided the TVS-owned company with its first major award since its revival. You might like to read our Norton Manx R review . Leading the design of the new superbike was Simon Skinner, Head of Design at Norton Motorcycles, who accepted the award on behalf of the company. signals.title: If you build it, they will come: Is the Harley-Davidson Sportster behind H-D stock rise?
signals.summary: Harley-Davidson is returning to its roots with the Sportster revival and more affordable models developed with Hero MotoCorp. Could that be helping turn its fortunes around? Harley-Davidson shares are rising, with the American motorcycle manufacturer enjoying its strongest stock market performance in more than a decade. While cost-cutting and a renewed focus on the brand's heritage are part of the story, two product lines could prove particularly important to its future: the returning Sportster 883 and a new generation of more affordable motorcycles. A recent Financial Times analysis points to Harley-Davidson's improving fortunes, with its share price up almost a third in 2026. The company's new boss, Artie Starrs, is attempting to turn things around by reconnecting with the brand's traditional strengths, while making its motorcycles more accessible to new customers. The return of the Sportster is a key part of that plan. Harley-Davidson discontinued its air-cooled Evolution-engined Sportsters in 2022, with emissions regulations making further development of the old platform increasingly difficult to justify. However, the company is bringing a proper air-cooled Sportster back for 2027, following a tsunami of requests from riders and dealers. It's an important move, not just because the Sportster has traditionally served as an entry point into Harley ownership, but also because it offers that familiar V-twin experience without the size and expense of the H-D’s heavyweights. Its return could give existing fans a reason to visit their dealers, while providing a more accessible route into the brand for new riders. But the Sportster isn't the only bike that could help Harley-Davidson reconnect with the market. The company is also expanding its entry-level offering, including motorcycles developed through its partnership with the vast Indian manufacturer Hero MotoCorp. The Harley-Davidson X440, developed with Hero and built in India, already demonstrates that approach. It’s a simple, low-cost single-cylinder machine, with weight and overall dimensions in line with most other A2 licence bikes on the market. That makes it a much more accessible machine than anything else in the Harley range. A new, more affordable model carrying the Sprint name is also planned, aimed at opening the door to customers who find the price of a larger Harley difficult to justify. That strategy makes sense in a global motorcycle market where much of the growth is coming from smaller, less expensive machines. Harley-Davidson has spent years churning out heavyweight cruisers and touring bikes, but that leaves it exposed to an ageing customer base and limits its ability to attract younger riders. Both of those factors have hit it hard in recent years. The company's average customer age is around 45, while its sales volumes remain well below the levels it achieved two decades ago. Lower-priced motorcycles could broaden its appeal, although competing in this part of the market will require careful attention to pricing, production costs and dealer margins. Whether that translates into sustained growth remains to be seen. A rising share price doesn't necessarily mean the turnaround is complete, and neither the revived Sportster nor a cheaper entry-level bike is guaranteed to become an instant sales success. Still, Harley-Davidson appears to be moving in the right direction with its more balanced range. And before those bikes have even been officially revealed, the stock market seems to show positive signs of recovery. signals.title: Alpinestars launches new Supertech R7 helmet
signals.summary: Alpinestars has launched the Supertech R7, a new full-face helmet with a composite shell, adjustable fit system and ECE 22.06 homologation. Alpinestars has expanded its Supertech helmet range with the launch of the Supertech R7 (S-R7), a full-face road helmet designed for road riding and track days. It sits below the existing S-R10 in the Italian brand’s helmet line-up and combines a multi-composite shell with a range of features aimed at impact protection, ventilation and fit adjustment. The S-R7 uses a shell made from carbon fibre, aramid and fibreglass, bonded with pre-preg epoxy resin. It is homologated to ECE 22.06 and US DOT standards, with a medium-sized helmet weighing a claimed 1,390g. Inside, the helmet uses a multi-density EPS liner made from seven sections across six densities, with three outer shell sizes used to accommodate different head sizes. Alpinestars has also incorporated its patented PLASMA technology, which uses a low-friction surface intended to help reduce rotational forces during an impact. The company claims the helmet exceeds the ECE 22.06 peak rotational acceleration standard by 80 per cent. The shell incorporates recesses around the collarbone area, housing PLASMA inserts designed to help absorb energy during an impact or slide. Alpinestars has also developed the helmet in a wind tunnel, with an integrated rear spoiler and lateral winglets intended to improve aerodynamic stability and reduce drag at speed. Ventilation comes from 10 ports, comprising six intakes and four exhausts. Three chin vents and three upper vents feed air into the helmet, while the chin vents also direct airflow towards the visor to help reduce fogging. The upper vent mechanism slides open to expose three internal air channels. The visor is an ECE 22.06-homologated Optical Class 1 unit with double-sided anti-scratch treatment. It has a tool-free quick-release mechanism and comes with a Pinlock 120 MaxVision anti-fog insert. Another feature is Alpinestars’ A-Head fitment system, which allows riders to adjust the helmet’s height and angle using a micro-adjustable pad connected to the EPS liner. The removable, washable lining includes antimicrobial-treated fabrics, while the cheek pads feature channels for eyewear, an emergency release system and provision for a hydration tube. The S-R7 is also ready for Alpinestars’ A-Connect communication system, which includes Mesh 3.0 intercom technology and Harman Kardon speakers. The helmet is now available in Europe through authorised Alpinestars dealers and online. Solid colours include matte black, gloss black, gloss grey and gloss white, alongside A-Core, Zeal, Kinetis and Lumen graphic designs. Each helmet comes with a clear visor, Pinlock 120 MaxVision insert, breath deflector, chin curtain and storage bag. signals.title: Shark SKWAL iCUP helmet gets integrated LED brake light
signals.summary: Shark has expanded its SKWAL helmet range with the iCUP, a full-face lid featuring an integrated LED signature and an accelerometer-operated F1-inspired brake light. Shark has expanded its LED-equipped helmet range with the launch of the SKWAL iCUP, a new full-face lid that takes design inspiration from Formula 1 with an integrated rear LED light that doubles as an automatic brake light. Already available in stores, the SKWAL iCUP will also be displayed at EICMA in Milan in November 2026, joining the existing SKWAL i3 and SKWAL i3 JET in the French manufacturer's line-up. The new helmet combines the sporty styling of Shark's SKWAL CUP with the lighting technology introduced on the SKWAL i3 in 2023. Its main visual feature is a vertical LED strip integrated into the rear spoiler, which illuminates red when activated. An integrated accelerometer detects deceleration and triggers the brake light automatically, without requiring a wired connection or Bluetooth link to the motorcycle. The system is designed to make the rider more visible to following traffic, and adds the additional benefit of having a brake light showing even when rolling off the throttle or when using engine braking. The lighting system offers three modes: position lights, smart brake lights and flashing lights. Shark claims battery life of up to 12 hours in flashing mode, with a full recharge taking approximately three hours. The SKWAL iCUP is built around a Lexan polycarbonate shell available in two shell sizes, with a multi-density EPS liner. It is approved to the ECE 22.06 helmet safety standard and features four air inlets, two exhaust vents, a Class 1 optical visor and a Pinlock 70 insert supplied as standard. A quick-release visor mechanism and an integrated anti-fog sun visor are also included. Other features include a removable inner lining, Shark's Easy Fit system for spectacle wearers and a Double D-ring fastening. The helmet is also ready for a SENA for Shark communication system. signals.title: New Section 59 rules mean police can seize motorcycles without issuing a warning first
signals.summary: The British Motorcyclists Federation has clarified new Section 59 powers, which allow police to seize motorcycles without warning that are being used anti-socially. Police in England and Wales can now seize motorcycles, and any other vehicles, being used anti-socially without issuing a warning first. The British Motorcyclists Federation (BMF) has published guidance explaining the changes, warning riders that they could lose access to their motorcycles immediately if their behaviour meets the legal threshold for seizure. Previously the police generally had to issue a warning before seizing a vehicle under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002, unless an exception applied. That requirement was removed on June 29, 2026, under the Crime and Policing Act 2026, giving officers greater scope to act against anti-social use of motorcycles and other vehicles. Section 59 applies where a uniformed police officer has reasonable grounds to believe a vehicle has been used in a careless or inconsiderate manner. It also covered unauthorised off-road riding. In all cases, though, it covered circumstances that caused, or are likely to cause, alarm, distress or annoyance to the public. Examples of that could be deemed as street racing, burnouts, aggressive riding, anti-social stunt riding and riding motorcycles on land where motor vehicles are not permitted. The rules surrounding seized vehicles have also changed. Since July 22, 2026, the statutory period before a vehicle can be disposed of has been reduced from 14 days to seven, making it important for owners to act quickly if their motorcycle is taken into police custody. However, the BMF is keen to stress that the changes do not give police unrestricted powers to seize motorcycles simply because an officer dislikes how they look or sound. An excessively loud exhaust or an undersized number plate can result in separate enforcement action, but neither automatically triggers Section 59. Noise could, however, form part of the wider circumstances if a rider is deliberately revving their motorcycle while behaving inconsiderately in a residential area. Simply riding a bike legally and within the scope of the law, which just happens to have a noisy pipe on it, isn’t enough to trigger it – in theory, at least. The federation has also reassured trail and green-lane riders that legitimate off-road riding remains legal, provided the route allows motor vehicle access and is not subject to restrictions such as a Traffic Regulation Order (TRO). For riders, the practical advice is straightforward enough, and in line with how most of us ride anyway. If you ride considerately, keep the motorcycle road-legal and check access rights before heading off-road, you’ll be fine. The guidance applies to England and Wales, with different legal provisions covering Scotland and Northern Ireland. signals.title: Kawasaki appears to be adding another adventure bike to its growing line-up
signals.summary: A new Kawasaki KLE650 SE has appeared in Australian type-approval documents, hinting that the revived KLE could be about to get a bigger sibling. Kawasaki looks to be working on another adventure bike for 2027, because apparently you can never have too many ADVs under one roof! The Japanese manufacturer has already revived the KLE name with its new KLE500 in 2026, but a recently spotted Australian type-approval listing suggests a larger KLE650 SE could be joining the range next year. The paperwork, dated October 16, identifies a machine carrying the LE650L type designation and the model name KLE 650 (SE), according to German publication Motorrad. There is no official announcement from Kawasaki yet, so exactly what the new model will look like, or where it will sit in the range, remains unclear. However, the registration does give us a fairly substantial clue that the firm could be planning to expand its true adventure bike offering beyond the 500cc class. The KLE name carries a lot of weight for Kawasaki, with the original KLE500 arriving in 1991 as a middleweight twin-cylinder machine with a 21-inch front wheel and an emphasis on versatility. Kawasaki brought the name back for its latest KLE500, which combines a 451cc parallel-twin engine with a chassis designed for both road riding and light off-road use. A larger KLE would make sense as a step up for riders wanting more capacity, although it would also put Kawasaki into a busy part of the adventure market. The existing Versys 650 already covers the road-focused touring side of the equation, with its 649cc parallel-twin engine and 17-inch wheels, leaving room for a more dirt-friendly machine if Kawasaki chooses to go down that route. The obvious question is whether the KLE650 SE would use the familiar 649cc parallel-twin engine found in the Ninja 650 and Versys 650, or whether Kawasaki has something else planned. That engine looks like a plausible candidate, but nothing in the type-approval listing confirms the specification, chassis or wheel sizes. For now, talk of a 21-inch front wheel, long-travel suspension or a more direct challenge to bikes such as the Yamaha Ténéré 700 remains speculation. It also begs the question: if Kawasaki is giving riders a stepping stone beyond the KLE500, where is the next step up after the KLE650? The Versys 1100 is Kawasaki’s range-topping adventure-style machine, although its wheels are honed firmly for riding on asphalt. If Kawasaki really wants to create a full-circle adventure bike range, a large-capacity option with true off-road credentials, like the Triumph Tiger 1200 or BMW R1300 GS, would be the cherry on top. Whatever happens with this story, it's clear that Kawasaki doesn’t appear to be putting all its adventure eggs in one pannier. signals.title: The French Arc Vector? Furion Taran revealed as 320bhp 2WD Tron bike
signals.summary: French firm Furion has revealed the Taran, an electric motorcycle with 326hp and drive to both wheels. It looks ambitious, but turning it into a viable production bike is harder than using ChatGPT to make pictures and videos. Back in 2018, a stealthy black electric bike boasting otherworldly performance figures, and an equally otherworldly price tag, was doing the rounds at EICMA. Fast forward to today, and the brand Arc is effectively no more, after going into liquidation in 2024. Arc’s failure to launch, after selling just eleven examples, wasn’t wholly unsurprising, given that electric bikes with a range of 200 miles and £90,000 price tags weren't, and still aren’t, really where the electric bike market is. One brand that doesn’t seem to have been listening to Arc’s story is Furion, as it is looking to finally make electric hyperbikes cool again. The Le Mans-based company has unveiled the Taran, an all-electric sportsbike that uses its EVERSOR technology to drive both wheels, with a motor integrated into the front hub. Furion claims the system can improve energy recovery under braking, increase range and improve agility, although those claims will need to be put to the test on a production-ready machine. The headline figures certainly look interesting. Furion quotes 240kW (326hp), a 20kWh battery, a weight of 230kg and a claimed real-world range of 200km (124 miles). That's a considerable amount of power for a motorcycle that weighs roughly the same as many conventional litre-class sportsbikes, although the battery capacity and claimed range suggest efficiency remains an important consideration. Furion says its EVERSOR technology has already been tested on a running prototype, with measurements taken at the Le Mans circuit used to calibrate its simulations. However, the company's current validation platform operates at 48 volts, with a move to 400 volts planned to unlock the system's full potential. The Taran's headline figures therefore need to be viewed in the context of a project that still has work to do before reaching customers. And that's where things get interesting. Furion has been developing unusual motorcycle technology for years. Its earlier M1 concept combined a rotary engine with electric assistance, while the subsequent M2 and F1 projects explored different ways of using a motor in the front wheel. The company has now shifted to an entirely electric architecture, with the Taran intended to demonstrate what its technology can achieve. There's nothing wrong with ambitious engineering, of course, but the motorcycle industry is littered with promising projects that struggled to make the leap from prototype to production. The obvious comparison is Britain's Arc Vector, an electric motorcycle packed with unusual engineering, premium materials and technology that aimed to set it apart from conventional bikes. Despite attracting considerable attention and eventually reaching customers, Arc's business entered liquidation in 2024. Its founder cited problems including US distribution and the difficulties of selling expensive, low-volume machines. Furion isn't necessarily following the same path, and its technology could ultimately find a home with established manufacturers through licensing. Indeed, the company says that supplying technology to other motorcycle makers is central to its business model, with the Taran intended as a limited-production showcase. However, Furion was reported in February 2026 to be seeking €2 million in funding to advance its electric motorcycle project. Its website is currently inviting people to register their interest in reservations and private tests, rather than offering a confirmed price or delivery date. That leaves plenty of questions unanswered, not least how much the Taran will cost, how much of its claimed performance can be sustained in real-world riding and whether customers will be willing to pay potentially large sums of money for its unusual engineering. The technology might prove worthwhile, but until Furion can demonstrate a finished motorcycle, a realistic price and a credible route to production, the Taran remains a promising proposition rather than a proven alternative to the electric bikes already on sale. The result was also a significant one for Husqvarna, representing the manufacturer's best Dakar Rally finish at the time. The initiative also has a charitable element, with part of the proceeds going to Fundación Nuestros Hijos, a Chilean organisation that supports children and young people with cancer and their families. The campaign is open to international buyers, although the website warns that any import costs, taxes, permits and other requirements will depend on the winner's country of residence. signals.title: At EICMA 2026 Maroil-Bardahl Italia spotlights top innovations, gear, and champions
signals.summary: Since 1973, Maroil has been developing and distributing Bardahl lubricants and additives across Italy, bringing the proud heritage of the renowned American brand to new heights. At EICMA 2026, the company invites passionate enthusiasts to Hall 14, Stand G20, to explore its complete lineup for the motorcycle sector , ranging from advanced engine formulations to dedicated maintenance equipment. Among the standout products on display is the XT4R 0W-50, a specialized racing lubricant born from an ongoing collaboration with the Barni Spark Racing Team , which has been officially confirmed for the upcoming year. Visitors can also discover Repower Moto , an advanced additive designed to clean internal components like valves, injectors, and combustion chambers, alongside the H2 Multicleaner Moto , an innovative hydrogen decarbonization tool for both two-stroke and four-stroke engines. The showcase is rounded out by the K9 line , dedicated to the deep cleaning and care of motorcycles and bicycles. The stand will also feature the brand-new apparel collection, blending urban culture with racing heritage, available for direct purchase at the fair. Adding to the excitement is Yari Montella's Ducati Panigale V4F SBK on display. To top it all off, an action-packed schedule of meet-and-greets awaits fans, featuring top motorsport stars and riders such as Alvaro Bautista and Michele Pirro. For real-time updates and all the latest news, make sure to follow Bardahl Italy's official social media channels. signals.title: Kawasaki KLE 500 SE: new Smartride clutch system and tubeless tyres
signals.summary: A year after the Kawasaki KLE 500 returned to the range, the Akashi-based manufacturer is expanding its mid-size crossover lineup. Making its debut at EICMA 2026 is the new SE Smartride version , which joins the standard and SE models. Its distinguishing feature is a new automatic centrifugal clutch. Put simply, when the bike comes to a stop, the Smartride clutch automatically disconnects the engine from the rear wheel. This means the rider no longer needs to keep the clutch lever pulled in when stopping in traffic and can safely engage first gear without the bike moving off or, worse, stalling. When it is time to pull away, all the rider needs to do is open the throttle: as engine revs rise, the clutch re-engages, ensuring smooth and precise take-offs. Once on the move, the rider can simply operate the clutch lever as usual. The KLE 500 SE Smartride is available exclusively in Pearl Blizzard White and features tubeless tyres, with a specific rear tyre size of 150/70-17. Like the other KLE versions, it can also be ordered with one of three special equipment packages: “ Rally”, “ Adventure Tourer” and “ Edition”. signals.title: RCB expands its range with new suspension and braking components
signals.summary: For the fourth consecutive year, RCB, a Malaysian brand specialising in high-performance components and accessories, is confirming its presence at EICMA. The company will be bringing a selection of new products to Milan, ranging from suspension and braking components to accessories. Among the products on display are the FD Series front fork, designed for the Yamaha XMAX and NVX, the S2+ ICE Alloy floating disc and a new carbon brake master cylinder. The latest RCB merchandise collection will also be on show, alongside some exclusive previews, which will be unveiled during the show itself. The stand will also feature a selection of components from UMA Racing, an Italian brand specialising in high-performance mechanical and electronic components. Solutions dedicated to the engine and performance will thus round off the RCB range. International stunt rider Rok Bagoroš will also be in attendance during the show. signals.title: Meet the F 450 RR: BMW's new supersport for A2 riders
signals.summary: BMW enters the segment of sport bikes that can be ridden with an A2 licence with the F 450 RR , which debuts at EICMA 2026. Its look is inspired by the S 1000 RR , with a lowered nose, raised tail, asymmetric fairings and aerodynamic winglets. The engine is the 420 cc parallel twin shared with the F 450 GS, delivering 48 hp and a maximum torque of 43 Nm. Claimed fuel consumption is 3.8 l/100 km, for a range of over 350 km. The steel trellis frame uses the engine as a stressed member, with a wheelbase of 1,450 mm. The chassis highlights are a 43 mm KYB upside-down fork (with adjustable damping on the Sport versions), a KYB rear shock and a 310 mm front disc with Brembo radial caliper. The electronics package includes ABS Pro with cornering function, Dynamic Brake Control and dynamic traction control. Weight is 177 kg ready to ride. Also standing out are three riding modes (Rain, Road, Race), a bidirectional electronic quickshifter (not on the Base) and a reversible shift pattern, a first for the segment. Four versions are available : Base (Cosmic Black), Sport (Racing Red), M Sport and M Sport with the Innovation package, which adds the Easy Ride Clutch automatic clutch. signals.title: Suzuki Buka Peluang Hadirkan Mobil Listrik Lebih Murah dari e Vitara
signals.summary: Suzuki Buka Peluang Hadirkan Mobil Listrik Lebih Murah dari e Vitara JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com PT Suzuki Indomobil Sales (SIS) belum mengungkapkan rencana menghadirkan mobil listrik dengan harga lebih terjangkau dibandingkan Suzuki e Vitara, yang saat ini ditawarkan mulai Rp 755 juta. Namun, perusahaan menyatakan terus memantau perkembangan pasar kendaraan listrik sebagai salah satu pertimbangan dalam menentukan arah pengembangan produk. Kehadiran mobil listrik dengan harga semakin kompetitif di Indonesia membuka peluang bagi produsen untuk menjangkau konsumen yang lebih luas. Suzuki sendiri telah memasarkan e Vitara sebagai salah satu model listriknya di Tanah Air. Baca juga: Daftar Provinsi yang Gelar Pemutihan PKB hingga Oktober 2026 Kompas.com/Donny Suzuki e Vitara di GIIAS 2025 Head of Sales 4W PT Suzuki Indomobil Sales (SIS) Rendy Anggadiputra mengatakan, riset pasar menjadi bagian dari pertimbangan perusahaan dalam menentukan produk yang akan dihadirkan ke depannya. Hasil riset dan studi pasar menjadi salah satu pertimbangan dalam menentukan arah pengembangan produk ke depannya, ujar Rendy kepada Kompas.com (19/10/2026). Pernyataan tersebut belum memastikan apakah Suzuki akan membawa mobil listrik dengan harga lebih rendah dari e Vitara. Meski demikian, perkembangan pasar dan kebutuhan konsumen menjadi faktor yang terus dipelajari perusahaan. Di pasar Jepang, mobil ini dibanderol mulai 2,12 juta yen atau sekitar Rp 230 jutaan. Harga tersebut membuat e-Sky menarik untuk dicermati apabila Suzuki mempertimbangkan ekspansi produk listrik ke segmen yang lebih terjangkau. Suzuki e-Sky memiliki panjang 3.395 milimeter, lebar 1.475 milimeter, dan tinggi 1.625 milimeter, mengikuti regulasi kendaraan kei car di Jepang. Berdasarkan pengujian WLTC, jarak tempuhnya diklaim mencapai 310 kilometer. Untuk pengisian daya, e-Sky mendukung pengisian AC 3,3 kW dengan waktu sekitar tujuh hingga delapan jam. Sementara itu, pengisian cepat DC 50 kW memungkinkan baterai terisi dari 20 persen menjadi 80 persen dalam sekitar 30 menit. Fitur lainnya mencakup Vehicle to Load (V2L) dengan daya hingga 1,5 kW, Vehicle to Home (V2H), layar infotainment 10,1 inci, dan panel instrumen digital 7 inci. signals.title: Omoda X Debut Global: Diklaim Mobil Pertama dengan Konsep Cross Off-Road
signals.summary: Omoda X Debut Global: Diklaim Mobil Pertama dengan Konsep Cross Off-Road WUHU, KOMPAS.com Omoda X resmi melakukan debut global pada 20 Oktober 2026 dalam acara Omoda X Night. Model terbaru dari Omoda ini mengusung konsep Cross Off-Road, yang memadukan kepraktisan SUV, karakter kendaraan off-road, serta tampilan dinamis mobil sport. Melalui konsep tersebut, Omoda X dikembangkan untuk konsumen yang menginginkan kendaraan dengan karakter berbeda. Mobil ini dirancang untuk menunjang aktivitas harian di perkotaan sekaligus menemani perjalanan luar ruang, seperti menuju pegunungan atau kawasan pantai. Omoda mengklaim X sebagai kendaraan pertama di dunia yang mengusung konsep Cross Off-Road . Model ini juga menjadi pengembangan terbaru dari tiga karakter utama merek tersebut, yakni MECHA yang menonjolkan desain futuristis, CROSS yang mengedepankan fleksibilitas, serta SMART yang berfokus pada teknologi pintar. Baca juga: Sudah Lengkap, Ini Daftar Pebalap MotoGP 2027 Dari segi desain mengadopsi gaya futuristis yang terinspirasi dari budaya mecha. Bagian eksterior memiliki postur bodi lebar, bahu kendaraan yang tegas, garis bodi menyempit di bagian tengah, serta siluet sporty. Sementara itu, penggunaan bentuk geometris dan lampu belakang menyerupai kilatan petir menjadi ciri khas tampilannya. Nuansa futuristis juga berlanjut ke bagian kabin. Omoda X menggunakan konsep MECHA Command Cockpit dengan tata letak dasbor menyerupai dua sayap dan konsol tengah mengambang berbentuk huruf X. Perangkat digitalnya terdiri dari panel instrumen berukuran 10,25 inci dan layar sentuh tengah 13,2 inci. Meski mengedepankan teknologi digital, Omoda tetap menyediakan tombol fisik untuk mengoperasikan sejumlah fungsi yang sering digunakan, seperti pengaturan AC dan mode berkendara. Pendekatan ini ditujukan untuk memadukan tampilan modern dengan kemudahan pengoperasian. Untuk menunjang aktivitas luar ruang, Omoda X memiliki ground clearance 200 mm dan kemampuan menerjang genangan air lebih dari 700 mm. Kendaraan ini juga diklaim memiliki kapasitas menarik beban hingga 1.800 kg, kapasitas beban atap 75 kg, serta 39 ruang penyimpanan untuk membawa berbagai perlengkapan aktivitas, termasuk sepeda dan peralatan selancar. Baca juga: Bukan Cuma Gaya, Ini Alasan Dashcam Makin Dicari Pemilik Mobil Dari sisi teknologi, Omoda X dilengkapi SIAS (Super Intelligent AI Space), sistem yang dikembangkan untuk memungkinkan interaksi lebih alami antara pengguna dan kendaraan. Sistem ini diklaim dapat memahami percakapan tanpa harus menggunakan kata aktivasi khusus atau perintah yang rumit. Tersedia juga X-MODE, mode berkendara personal yang memungkinkan pengaturan kendaraan dan respons performa disesuaikan dengan preferensi pengemudi. Untuk membantu berkendara malam hari, Omoda X menggunakan sistem penglihatan malam berbasis pencitraan termal inframerah yang diklaim dapat membantu mendeteksi potensi bahaya hingga jarak 90 meter. Fitur hiburan juga menjadi bagian dari pengembangan mobil ini. Omoda X Open Mic memungkinkan penumpang berkaraoke di dalam kabin menggunakan empat zona penangkap suara terpisah tanpa mikrofon genggam. Selain itu, tersedia aksesori MECHA Pets berbasis NFC magnetik yang dirancang untuk menambah unsur interaktif selama perjalanan. signals.title: Berapa Lama Bensin Bertahan di Tangki Mobil Jarang Dipakai?
signals.summary: Berapa Lama Bensin Bertahan di Tangki Mobil Jarang Dipakai? JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Ketika pasokan bahan bakar minyak (BBM) sulit didapat, pemilik mobil mungkin memilih mengurangi penggunaan kendaraan agar bensin yang tersisa di tangki bisa bertahan lebih lama. Namun, mobil yang terlalu lama tidak digunakan juga perlu mendapat perhatian, terutama terkait kualitas bahan bakar yang tersimpan di dalam tangki. Lantas, berapa lama bensin bisa bertahan di dalam tangki mobil yang jarang digunakan? Baca juga: Alasan Mayoritas Pemilik Mobil Ganti Head Unit Android Dosen Teknik Mesin Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) Jayan Sentanuhady mengatakan, BBM yang disimpan oleh konsumen masih bisa ditoleransi selama tiga sampai enam bulan. Tergantung penyimpan dan jenisnya, umumnya BBM yang mengandung nabati seperti biosolar dan etanol lebih cepat mengalami degradasi, ucap Jayan kepada Kompas.com, belum lama ini. KOMPAS.COM/SUCI RAHAYU Tangki bahan bakar untuk milik produk baru BYD M6 DM sudah ada di Surabaya yang menjadi salah satu kota yang mendapat perhatian besar dari PT BYD Motor Indonesia karena dinilai memiliki peran penting dalam mendorong pertumbuhan kendaraan elektrifikasi di kawasan timur Indonesia. Namun, lama penyimpanan BBM tidak bisa disamaratakan karena bergantung pada jenis bahan bakar dan kondisi tempat penyimpanannya. Menurut Jayan, tempat penyimpanan yang ideal adalah tangki yang kedap udara. Namun, kondisi tersebut tidak sepenuhnya memungkinkan pada tangki BBM kendaraan karena terdapat lubang ventilasi udara. Kondisi tersebut membuat kualitas bahan bakar perlu diperhatikan ketika mobil jarang digunakan dalam waktu lama. Baca juga: Cerita Pengguna, Pengalaman 3 Tahun Pakai Honda Revo Tenaga Listrik Sapta Agung Nugraha Auto2000 Tutup tangki mobil mesin diesel Kondisi tangki dan lingkungan penyimpanan turut memengaruhi kualitas bahan bakar ketika mobil jarang digunakan dalam waktu lama. Pemilik bengkel spesialis Toyota Mitsubishi, Garasi Auto Service, Muchlis, mengatakan, terdapat beberapa faktor yang dapat membuat kualitas BBM turun lebih cepat, salah satunya paparan udara. Pertama BBM terpapar udara, ini akan memicu terjadinya oksidasi dalam jumlah banyak, bila tangki atau wadah tidak rapat, BBM akan bereaksi dengan oksigen, ucap Muchlis kepada Kompas.com. Selain paparan udara, suhu penyimpanan juga turut memengaruhi kualitas BBM. Jika BBM terkena panas dari sinar matahari langsung, suhu tinggi dapat mempercepat reaksi kimia sehingga bensin lebih cepat menguap dan nilai oktannya turun. signals.title: Daftar Pebalap Senior yang Tinggalkan MotoGP di Musim 2027
signals.summary: Daftar Pebalap Senior yang Tinggalkan MotoGP di Musim 2027 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Sejumlah pebalap dipastikan tidak akan tampil lagi di ajang MotoGP pada musim 2027. Perubahan susunan pebalap membuat lima nama yang sudah cukup lama berkompetisi di kelas premier harus mengakhiri kiprahnya di kejuaraan tersebut. Kelima pebalap itu adalah Maverick Vinales, Alex Rins, Jack Miller, Brad Binder, dan Franco Morbidelli. AFP/LLUIS GENE Pebalap Aprilia Racing, Maverick Vinales, saat konferensi pers menjelang MotoGP Aragon 2021 di Sirkuit MotorLand Aragon, Kamis (9/9/2021). Mereka memiliki pengalaman panjang di kejuaraan dunia balap motor, termasuk meraih kemenangan di kelas MotoGP. Perubahan tersebut menjadi bagian dari perombakan besar susunan pebalap menjelang musim 2027. Sejumlah tim memilih merekrut pebalap baru, termasuk pebalap yang naik kelas dari Moto2. Maverick Vinales menjadi salah satu pebalap yang tidak memiliki kursi di MotoGP untuk musim 2027. Baca juga: Sudah Lengkap, Ini Daftar Pebalap MotoGP 2027 AFP/JAVIER SORIANO Pebalap asal Spanyol Alex Rins merayakan kemenangan pada balapan terakhir bersama Suzuki Ecstar. Balapan terakhir Alex Rins bersama Suzuki Ecstar jatuh pada MotoGP Valencia 2022 yang berlangsung di Sirkuit Ricardo Tormo, Minggu (6/11/2022) malam WIB. Pebalap asal Spanyol itu mengakhiri kiprahnya bersama Tech3 KTM setelah menjalani karier panjang di kelas premier. Vinales tercatat meraih 10 kemenangan di MotoGP dan total 26 kemenangan di tiga kelas kejuaraan dunia. Ia juga pernah meraih gelar juara dunia Moto3 pada 2013. Meski tidak melanjutkan karier di MotoGP, Vinales belum memastikan akan beralih ke World Superbike (WorldSBK). Ia bahkan menegaskan tidak memiliki rencana untuk berkompetisi di kejuaraan tersebut. Dengan demikian, masa depan Vinales di dunia balap motor masih belum sepenuhnya jelas setelah musim 2026 berakhir. Baca juga: Update Daftar Pebalap MotoGP 2027, Moreira Resmi Masuk HRC Castrol Dok. Yamaha Jack Miller dan Yamaha Racing Team akan bersaing di Suzuka 8 Hours Endurance Race 2025 Alex Rins juga tidak akan melanjutkan kiprahnya di MotoGP pada 2027.
